notes.text: Greek τύπος. Given the many early traditions that the sin of Baal-Peor involved sexual practices, our rendering of the LJLA usage in this context is undoubtedly insufficient. Whatever the Moabite women were displaying beneath their skirts ended up seducing the Israelites. Perhaps we are dealing here rather with a euphemism for vagina (i.e., "mold"), thus טופסיה דפעור is intended to mean something like "wide open vagina".

notes.text: To judge by etymology, "young lamb" is the original meaning of this word (compare American "kid"), but that usage has almost totally disappeared from Aramaic other than in Jewish texts where all the examples can easily be taken to be Hebraisms. The scarcity of the meaning "lamb" in Aramaic was pointed out to us by Prof. Ed Cook. Note from the examples that the age range of such youths normally can be anywhere from infancy to older teen-age, but for a substantial outlier (30-40 years!) see Am7 110:11.
